business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain's bilateral investment treaties and double taxation agreements apply according to the counterparty, entry-into-force status, territorial scope, and any applicable termination or replacement provisions; the investor's country of origin is not specified, so no individual treaty can be confirmed as applicable.
EU internal-market rules and applicable EU trade agreements may govern relevant cross-border activity; they are not, by themselves, bilateral investment treaties.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, particularly Articles 3–4; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May implementing Law 10/2010; and Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales, RCTIR). The general beneficial-owner test is a natural person holding, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of the capital or voting rights, or otherwise exercising control; where none is identified, the senior managing official is recorded under the statutory fallback. Companies must obtain, maintain, and update beneficial-ownership information and provide it to competent authorities and obliged entities. Access to the RCTIR is governed by applicable law and is not unrestricted public access.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder's certificate of incorporation, current registry extract, constitutional documents, and evidence of authority to invest
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or other competent public authority in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing country and document qualify under the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise Spanish consular legalization, subject to any applicable treaty exemption

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign shareholder's board resolution or equivalent authorization approving incorporation and appointing an authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder's competent corporate body; notarization by a competent notary where required for authentication
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if eligible; otherwise Spanish consular legalization; sworn translation into Spanish where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document and Spanish tax identification documentation for each foreign individual founder, administrator, and relevant beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent identity or tax authority in the individual's country of residence or nationality; Spanish tax identification number issued by the Spanish Tax Agency where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Identity-document authentication depends on the document and receiving authority; public foreign documents requiring formal use in Spain must be apostilled or consularly legalized unless exempt; sworn Spanish translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the Spanish incorporation, execution, and tax-registration formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal before a competent notary or other legally authorized official in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if eligible; otherwise Spanish consular legalization; sworn translation into Spanish where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial-ownership declaration and ownership-and-control chart, supported by evidence tracing ownership to natural persons
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign and Spanish shareholders, with supporting extracts from competent corporate registries and other relevant records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Supporting foreign public documents apostilled or consularly legalized where required; notarization is not a universal statutory requirement for the chart itself

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Spanish obliged entities must apply risk-based customer due diligence under Law 10/2010 and Royal Decree 304/2014, identify beneficial owners, assess source of funds and purpose of the relationship, and apply enhanced measures to politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and known close associates as prescribed by law. Screen relevant parties and transactions against applicable EU restrictive measures and UN Security Council sanctions. OFAC screening is not a general Spanish statutory requirement but may be required by US nexus, correspondent banks, contractual policy, or risk controls. Check current Spanish and EU national measures and applicable sectoral export-control restrictions; retain evidence of screening and escalation decisions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online name-certification service (Certificación negativa de denominación social)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be distinct and comply with Spanish company-name rules and the Regulations of the Mercantile Register. The name must include or be accompanied by the legal-form indication Sociedad Limitada, Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, S.L., or S.R.L. Names may use foreign-language terms subject to distinctiveness and public-order rules. A foreign-language or transliterated name does not dispense with the required legal-form indication. The RMC determines acceptability; trademark clearance is separate and should also be conducted with the Spanish Patent and Trademark Office and, where relevant, EUIPO.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying a public authority, government body, or official status without authorization

Terms whose use is legally reserved or regulated, including certain banking, insurance, securities, professional, and other regulated-sector designations, unless the required authorization or legal conditions are met
Terms contrary to law, public order, or good customs
Names identical to or confusingly similar to existing registered company names, subject to RMC rules
Names suggesting an activity or status the company is not authorized or entitled to conduct
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative name certificate reserves the approved denomination for six months from issue; the certificate's use for execution of the incorporation deed is subject to its separate three-month validity. Confirm both dates directly on the certificate and obtain a renewed certificate if required. The standard procedure is to submit a new or amended name application, addressing the RMC's stated objection and supplying supporting material. For a formal adverse decision, use the administrative or registry appeal route stated in the notification and applicable Mercantile Registry Regulations, observing the stated deadline; seek review by the Directorate General responsible for legal security and public faith where available. A name certificate does not confer trademark rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Spanish Companies Act (Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010). A virtual-office address is not categorically prohibited if it is a genuine, legally usable registered-office address and satisfies registry, tax, and service-of-process requirements. For wholesale semiconductor trading, a virtual office alone may be inadequate for banking onboarding, tax residence and substance evidence, inventory operations, customs records, or counterparties' due diligence. Document actual decision-making, personnel, contracts, accounting, inventory or third-party logistics arrangements, and the authority to use the address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official or reliable industry-specific probability of unannounced inspections is published; a numerical likelihood cannot be stated. Risk is fact-dependent and may increase with VAT refund claims, intra-EU goods movements, import/export activity, high-risk counterparties, address inconsistencies, or AML and tax alerts. Maintain accessible corporate, accounting, inventory, transport, and beneficial-ownership records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry incorporation filing and registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative statutory-tariff estimate; exact amount depends on filing particulars and registry charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Spanish tax identification number applications and administrative processing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) and, where applicable, intermediary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tax identification issuance is generally not subject to a material government fee; estimate covers document preparation or service-provider charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign corporate-document notarization, apostilles, or consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign notary, apostille authority, or Spanish consular authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative range midpoint; fees depend on country, document count, urgency, and applicable treaty exemptions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translations of foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish sworn translator or other translator accepted by the receiving authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market estimate by word count, document complexity, and certification requirements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal, corporate, UBO, and AML due-diligence review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish corporate counsel or compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative professional-services benchmark; scope and cross-border ownership complexity drive fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Patent and Trademark Office, EUIPO, or professional search provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative market estimate; basic database searches may have no official fee, while professional clearance is chargeable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office or commercial domicile setup for the initial period
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative market benchmark; varies by city, service level, and whether a physical office is used

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank onboarding, source-of-funds documentation, and payment-rail preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Selected bank or payment service provider and any professional adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative service-provider and advisory estimate; account approval and charges are institution-specific

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), including Articles 4 (minimum capital), 20–23 (formation and articles), 31–33 (execution and effectiveness of incorporation), and 62–63 (capital contributions). Law 14/2013 of 27 September and applicable implementing rules govern electronic formation through CIRCE.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office; the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) issues the company-name clearance certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), filed for registration in the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital for an SL is EUR 1. Contributions must be fully assumed and paid at formation. Until share capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve, and shareholders are jointly and severally liable for the difference between EUR 3,000 and subscribed capital if the company is liquidated with insufficient assets. No statutory escrow account is required. A bank certificate may evidence cash contributions; non-cash contributions require a description and valuation in the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in the incorporation deed and confirms that the subscribed shares have been fully paid as stated therein. RESOLVED, that the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted, subject to registration and any required shareholder approval. RESOLVED, that [name and identification number] is appointed [sole director/joint directors/board member] and [name] is appointed [managing director/secretary], each subject to the articles and applicable law. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers are authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, complete tax and registry formalities, open operating bank accounts, and make required commercial and administrative registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), company-name certificate service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a negative company-name certificate, listing alternative names in order of preference. The certificate must identify the proposed founder or a person authorized by the founder and be valid when the incorporation deed is executed. Submit electronically through the Registry’s official service or through a notary/CIRCE.
required_dossiers: Applicant identification and authorization, if applicable
Proposed company form and applicant contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is unavailable or rejected, submit alternative names and obtain a replacement certificate before executing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain tax identification and prepare the incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT); CIRCE/Entrepreneur Service Points may coordinate electronic formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Spanish tax identification number (NIF) for each foreign founder or director where required, and request the company’s provisional NIF using Form 036 after execution of the deed or through the available electronic formation workflow. Prepare the articles, registered-office details, business purpose, share allocation, management structure, and capital contribution evidence. Foreign documents must be apostilled or legalized as applicable and accompanied by a sworn Spanish translation where required.
required_dossiers: Founder and director identification documents and NIFs
Powers of attorney and legalized corporate documents for entity founders, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete NIF applications or documentary defects with AEAT. Replace expired name certificates and provide apostilled/legalized originals and sworn translations when requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario); CIRCE may coordinate notarial execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or duly empowered representatives execute the public deed before a Spanish notary. State the company name, registered office, business purpose, capital, share allocation, contributions, and initial management appointments. Pay the capital in full; provide bank evidence for cash contributions if requested, or identify and describe non-cash contributions in the deed. The notary submits the deed electronically where available.
required_dossiers: Founder and representative identification and NIFs
Proof of authority and legalized corporate documents for entity founders
Cash contribution evidence or non-cash contribution descriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve notarial objections by correcting the articles, proving authority or identity, or supplying missing contribution evidence; re-execute or rectify the deed as directed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company and complete tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry for the registered office; AEAT for tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed and required supporting documents with the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry within the applicable filing period. Obtain the registration entry and permanent NIF. Submit or complete Form 036 to register tax and census particulars, including the activity, commencement date, VAT position, and relevant tax elections. Incorporation is effective as a registered company upon registration.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIF and completed tax census information
Evidence of applicable tax filings or exemptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a qualification notice, cure the stated defect within the statutory period by filing corrected documents or a rectifying deed. Challenge a qualification through the statutory registry appeal process where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete local commercial and premises formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal authority (Ayuntamiento) for the registered and operating premises; regional authority where regional rules apply
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing activity at a warehouse, office, or other premises, confirm zoning compatibility and determine whether a municipal responsible declaration (declaración responsable), prior communication (comunicación previa), or activity and works authorization is required. Register the business activity and premises as required. A wholesale trading company without manufacturing operations does not generally require a national industrial operating licence.
required_dossiers: Company deed, registry details, and NIF
Technical certificate or project where required by the municipality
Fire-safety and accessibility documentation where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to municipal requests with amended plans, technical certifications, or additional filings. Suspend use of affected premises until mandatory authorization or corrective works are completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete employer and commercial registrations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Social Security General Treasury (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social); AEAT; applicable regional or municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before hiring employees, obtain an employer contribution account code and register the company and employees with Social Security. Maintain statutory accounting books and file them with the Mercantile Registry in accordance with applicable deadlines. Assess separate product, import, customs, waste, and packaging obligations based on the products handled and the company’s role in placing them on the Spanish market.
required_dossiers: Accounting records and required corporate books
Product, import, and supply-chain compliance records, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete Social Security or registry submissions promptly and regularize any missed employer, accounting, or product-compliance filing before continued operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No national industrial licensing board approval is generally required for wholesale brokerage of SSDs and server processors without manufacturing or regulated industrial processes. The competent municipal authority governs premises activity and works formalities; the relevant Autonomous Community industrial authority applies only if a regulated installation or industrial activity is introduced.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific national manufacturing or industrial operating permit generally applies. A premises-specific municipal responsible declaration (declaración responsable), prior communication (comunicación previa), or activity licence may be required, depending on the municipality, premises, and activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico) is the national authority where national competence applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary wholesale trading and warehousing without manufacturing, significant installations, or listed development. Confirm screening requirements against Law 21/2013 and the applicable Autonomous Community rules for the specific premises and project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or manufacturing VOC limits ordinarily arise from wholesale trading alone. Any discharge must comply with the applicable municipal sewer bylaw and discharge authorization; emissions from any installed equipment must meet applicable regional and national rules. Waste must be segregated and managed through authorized operators under Law 7/2022. Electrical and electronic equipment, batteries, packaging, and related waste obligations may apply according to the company’s role as producer, importer, or distributor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No general national pre-operation civil-defence certificate applies solely to wholesale trading. The premises must satisfy applicable building, fire-safety, accessibility, and occupational-risk requirements; municipal activity procedures may require a competent technical certificate or project, fire-safety documentation, and structural or load verification based on the premises and stored goods. Employers must comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention and implementing rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. The AEAT administers the Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIF), Corporate Income Tax, Value Added Tax, Intrastat and related registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a definitive NIF from the AEAT after incorporation and registration with the Commercial Registry. The incorporation file normally includes the public deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry evidence, registered office, corporate purpose, identification of directors and beneficial owners, and powers of attorney where applicable. A provisional NIF may be requested during formation using Form 036, followed by submission of the definitive registration evidence. Foreign shareholders, directors and authorized representatives generally require Spanish NIFs for tax and corporate filings; non-resident individuals commonly obtain an NIE, while non-resident legal entities obtain an NIF through the AEAT using Form 036 and supporting constitutional, tax-residence and representation documents. The company must file Form 036 to register in the census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholding agents, state its VAT activities and communicate its tax address. For intra-Community acquisitions or supplies, the company must request registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and obtain an ES-prefixed VAT identification number. VIES validation should be completed before applying intra-Community exemptions. Electronic filing generally requires an AEAT digital certificate or an authorized representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is generally subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal taxpayer; Spain does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL to elect transparent or disregarded treatment. Tax consolidation may be elected by qualifying Spanish-resident companies and qualifying permanent establishments within a group, subject to statutory ownership, control, filing and timing conditions. The company may also access specific statutory regimes, including the special regime for newly created entities where applicable, the reduced-size-entity regime where applicable, and other sector-specific or restructuring regimes. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD II apply by operation of law and are not elective. The tax treatment of a foreign-owned SL may also be affected by controlled foreign company, transfer pricing, beneficial ownership, withholding tax and treaty rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, or IVA), governed principally by Law 37/1992 and related regulations. Spanish VAT applies in mainland Spain and the Balearic Islands. The Canary Islands operate the separate IGIC system, while Ceuta and Melilla are outside the territorial scope of Spanish VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic VAT turnover threshold applies in Spain. A business carrying out taxable supplies in the Spanish VAT territory must register and comply from the commencement of the relevant economic activity or taxable transaction, subject to applicable exemptions and special regimes. The €85,000 EU SME exemption threshold is not currently a general Spanish domestic registration threshold. Separate registration may be required for intra-Community transactions, imports, distance sales, marketplaces, warehousing or other cross-border activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spanish invoices must satisfy formal requirements, including issuer and customer identification, NIF or VAT number where required, invoice number and date, description, taxable base, VAT rate and amount, and applicable exemption or reverse-charge wording. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, or SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including businesses exceeding the applicable turnover threshold, VAT groups and REDEME registrants, to electronically transmit specified invoice-register data to the AEAT generally within four business days, subject to statutory adjustments. SII is a transaction-data reporting system and is not a universal real-time pre-clearance requirement for all businesses. Spain's Law 18/2022 on business creation and growth establishes phased B2B electronic invoicing obligations, whose operative timing depends on implementing regulations. Royal Decree 1007/2023 establishes technical requirements for computerized invoicing systems and the VERI*FACTU framework, with implementation deadlines subject to the applicable transitional rules and subsequent amendments. Electronic records must preserve integrity, authenticity, traceability and auditability; unauthorized alteration, omission or destruction can trigger tax penalties. Electronic customs declarations are submitted through the AEAT customs systems and the EU customs platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with a right of deduction under the Spanish VAT Law, provided the seller or an authorized intermediary can substantiate the export and the goods actually leave the EU customs territory. The claim requires a valid customs export declaration and reliable evidence of exit, linked to the commercial invoice and transport documentation. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for VAT exemption rather than domestic zero-rating where the goods are transported to another EU Member State, the customer has a valid VAT identification number in another Member State, the supplier verifies and reports the transaction, and the transport and recapitulative-statement requirements are satisfied. Services supplied to non-EU customers are not automatically zero-rated; the place-of-supply rules must be applied. B2B services are commonly taxed where the customer is established and may be outside Spanish VAT, while specific use-and-enjoyment, immovable-property, passenger transport, admission, intermediary and other special rules can override the general rule. Input VAT refunds are generally claimed through periodic VAT returns by established businesses. Non-established businesses use the applicable refund procedure, including the EU electronic refund mechanism or the non-EU procedure under the statutory reciprocity and other eligibility conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Export Administrative Document or equivalent export customs declaration, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
AEAT or EU customs release and exit confirmation, such as the electronic exit result or equivalent proof that the goods left the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the seller, buyer, goods, value, delivery terms and export transaction
Packing list and product description sufficient to reconcile the shipment with the customs declaration
Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or other transport document
Purchase order, sales contract and delivery or acceptance evidence where required to establish the transaction chain
Evidence linking the customs declaration, transport document, invoice, goods and recipient
Import clearance or destination-country customs evidence where relevant and commercially available
Payment records or bank evidence where relevant to substantiate the underlying supply; a Spanish inward-remittance certificate is not a general statutory prerequisite for VAT export exemption
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification evidence, transport proof to the other Member State, and accurate EC Sales List reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for VAT export exemption. Export VAT treatment depends principally on proof of dispatch or transport outside the EU and customs exit, not on a fixed foreign-exchange repatriation period. The AEAT may deny or claw back the exemption and assess unpaid VAT, late-payment interest and applicable penalties where export conditions are not met, exit cannot be evidenced, documents are inconsistent, goods were diverted to the Spanish or EU market, or the transaction is fictitious. Tax penalties may be imposed for incorrect or incomplete tax returns, failure to issue compliant invoices, obstruction of inspection, inaccurate customs declarations and fraudulent conduct. Serious or intentional cases may involve enhanced penalties, customs debt, seizure or forfeiture measures, and criminal tax or customs exposure where statutory thresholds and intent requirements are met. A voluntary correction before formal inspection may reduce exposure under applicable Spanish penalty rules; documentary retention and consistent reconciliation of invoices, customs records, transport evidence, inventory and payment records are essential.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism, together with the Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation as the competent authorities for balance-of-payments statistics and external transactions reporting. Spain has no separate foreign exchange administration agency; the Bank of Spain supervises all resident credit institutions and authorized electronic money institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility is guaranteed for both current and capital account transactions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Spanish Law 19/2003 on capital movements. No prior administrative authorization is required for inward equity injections, trade remittances, loan repayments, or profit distributions. The only substantive compliance gates are (i) balance-of-payments statistical declarations (S-1/S-2 forms) for transactions with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000, (ii) AML/CFT and sanctions screening, and (iii) tax withholding procedures. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to corporate income tax settlement and, where applicable, the non-resident income tax withholding return (form 216) at the applicable double tax treaty rate (generally 10-15% for treaty jurisdictions and 19% for non-treaty jurisdictions). There are no dividend quotas, remittance licenses, or reinvestment obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion regime for export proceeds. A Spanish exporter may freely hold, in EUR or any foreign currency, the proceeds from sales of goods or services. The only statutory requirement is declaratory: transactions with non-resident counterparties equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000 (or cumulative quarterly thresholds) must be submitted to the Banco de España via the S-1 statistical declaration within the month following the operation, classifying the transaction under the balance-of-payments goods code. No conversion ratio or sales foreign-exchange timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Desembolso/Escrow) and Operational Account
Operational Account with dedicated USD correspondent routing and commercial LC desk
Operational Account and Escrow sub-account for trade inspection releases

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary clearing channel but Low as the primary treasury bank for escrow and LC-backed settlement. An EU-authorized Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensed under Law 21/2011 and Directive 2009/110/EC, or an EEA EMI passporting into Spain, may open a commercial payment account and execute SEPA/MT103-equivalent cross-border credit transfers with a minimum capital of EUR 350,000. However, EMIs are legally prohibited from granting credit, holding escrow-linked inspection funds as regulated custody, or issuing documentary letters of credit. Additionally, Spanish AML Law 10/2010 requires EMIs to execute the same UBO, source-of-funds, and OFAC/EU sanctions screening as banks, which effectively eliminates any speed advantage for high-value semiconductor transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video onboarding is permitted under EBA Guidelines on remote customer onboarding, but the Tier-1 Spanish banks in practice require at least one appointed director or the sole administrator to attend a face-to-face interview at the branch of account before activation for a Spanish SL. For EEA-resident directors, video-identification plus apostilled corporate documents may suffice at Santander and CaixaBank, reducing onboarding to 10-15 business days. For non-EEA directors, physical presence in Madrid or Barcelona is effectively mandatory, or in the alternative a notarized power of attorney granted to a Spanish resident attorney-in-fact is accepted, with all corporate documents apostilled by the jurisdiction of origin and translated by a sworn translator (traductor jurado).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain obscurity or intermediate holding vehicles in weak-AML or non-cooperative jurisdictions, combined with high-value and high-frequency CPU/SSD trade flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled UBO declaration, full chain-of-title registry extracts from the Registro Mercantil, deed of incorporation of every intermediate entity, audited financial statements for the ultimate beneficial owners, and a formal written explanation of the commercial rationale for each holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared paid-in capital and the volume of the first equity injection or trade disbursement, raising trade-based money laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase or equity injection, source-of-funds evidence from the foreign investor (audited balance sheet, asset sale contract, or bank reference), a signed master distribution agreement for the SSD/CPU goods, and the first confirmed purchase order with proforma invoice and Incoterms 2020 terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use export-control exposure: high-performance processors and storage devices may fall under EU Regulation 2021/821, and the bank flags transactions with buyers in sanctions-sensitive regions or with military-linked end users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Restricted-party screening log evidencing the use of an integrated EU/OFAC/UN sanctions database, a final-user and end-use certificate from each client, a formal declaration that the goods do not require an export authorization (or a copy of the valid SGAE export license if required), and a contractual clause imposing an end-use control covenant on the buyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected rapid settlement turnaround with daily large-volume outbound wires to foreign suppliers inconsistent with a de-novo entity's operational footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury cash-flow forecast tied directly to confirmed purchase orders, an escrow inspection agreement with an independent third-party inspector (e.g., SGS or Bureau Veritas) with a 30%/70% payment split, invoice-level forensic documentation (brand, model, serial numbers, unit price, quantities), customs clearance proof (DUA/ENS), and a prior bank reference from the counterparty's financial institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing structure: (i) the non-resident shareholder wires funds via SWIFT MT103 using the Banco de España balance-of-payments concept code 507 (Direct investment - equity capital from non-residents) and a transparent reference such as 'Equity contribution to capital increase - ES_SL'; (ii) the receiving Spanish bank pre-clears the inward credit against the notarized Spanish deed of capital increase inscribed in the Registro Mercantil; (iii) the funds are credited to a blocked capital disbursement account (cuenta de desembolso) and are not available for operations until the compliance team receives the certificate of the capital increase registration, the definitive CIF/NIE documentation of the foreign investor, and a certificate of the investor's authority; (iv) the bank automatically files the S-1 statistical declaration. The entire cycle typically takes 5-10 business days, and the funds may remain unavailable for up to 30 days if the deed registration is delayed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier settlements against signed trade invoices, with the S-1 statistical declaration identifying the beneficiary country and currency; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700 advised / MT710 negotiation or MT760 guarantee) for high-value CPU/SSD cargo, issued by the Spanish bank in favor of the overseas supplier with presentation of shipping documents at the advising bank; (3) Escrow-inspection wire structure - a 30% mobilization payment upon proforma invoice, with the remaining 70% held in a bank escrow sub-account and released only against a final inspection certificate issued by an independent surveyor, ensuring that the Swift_TT and Escrow_Inspection_Wire rails are both fully documented for AML reconstruction; (4) Documentary Collections (documents against payment / documents against acceptance) for better-established counterparties. All outbound wires above EUR 50,000 are reported to the Banco de España under the monthly S-1 declaration, and funds must be traceable to the underlying commercial contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the Spanish CMOF (Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras) framework - permitted for documented trade flows
FX Swaps (spot vs forward combination) for rolling short-term liquidity mismatches up to 12 months
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) restricted to currencies without full convertibility (e.g., ARS, COP, MXN) booked through the bank's offshore booking center to hedge Latin American client receivables
OTC European FX Options (calls and puts) on EUR/USD and EUR/CNY to cap procurement cost while retaining upside
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CIRS) for matched funding if the Spanish SL receives USD-denominated supplier credit or holds a USD-linked balance sheet exposure

All instruments are subject to EMIR (EU Regulation 648/2012) trade reporting and, where the counterparty is a financial entity, the clearing obligation; the SL should confirm its status as a non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold to minimize collateral posting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year end (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine under LSC Art. 200 up to EUR 60,000; closure of registration sheet if filings are omitted for three consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months and twenty-five days after fiscal year end (e.g., by 25 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 5%–20% plus late interest; administrative penalty up to EUR 1,500; possible penalty of 50% of amounts improperly claimed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Legalization of Statutory Books (Libros Registro)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year end (e.g., by 30 April for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 2,000; subsequent registry filings may be rejected until regularization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Informative Return for Third-Party Transactions (Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 28 February of the following calendar year for transactions exceeding EUR 3,005.06
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties from EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 per omitted or incorrect set of data, plus late interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Registry Confirmation (Declaración de Titularidad Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with Annual Accounts deposit (within six months after fiscal year end); update within 30 days of any UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sanctions under Law 10/2010: fines from EUR 600 to EUR 60,000 for failure to file or maintain accurate UBO information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit mandatory for SLs exceeding at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net revenue > EUR 8,000,000; average employees > 50. Audit also required where group consolidation, parent guarantees, or sector legislation applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable) under the Código de Comercio and Real Decreto 1514/2007; IFRS mandated for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must identify and file ultimate beneficial owners (ownership ≥25%). The Declaración de Titularidad Real is submitted annually together with the Annual Accounts; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the Mercantile Registry within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for newly created entities in the first two taxable periods with positive tax base (subject to certain conditions). Reduced rate of 20% for entities with a taxable turnover of less than EUR 1,000,000 per annum under the reduced-size entity regime (incentivos para entidades de reducida dimensión). Tax credits available for R&D activities (deducción por actividades de investigación y desarrollo e innovación tecnológica), export promotion activities, job creation for disabled workers, and reinvestment of extraordinary profits. Partial exemption under the special regime for holdings of foreign entities (régimen de entidades de tenencia de valores extranjeros, ETVE) for qualifying foreign-source dividends and capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Electronic filing mandatory through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) online portal using a digital certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or authorized representative (apoderado). The model 200 is filed annually with an information declaration and tax settlement integrated in the same form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year (i.e., for a 31 December year-end, filing deadline is 25 July of the following year). Actual tax year may differ if the company was newly incorporated (first tax period may exceed 12 months). The tax return must be filed within 25 days after the end of the statutory six-month filing window; payment of the resulting tax liability is due simultaneously with the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF), corporate name, and registered address of the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish SL with non-resident shareholders must provide the entity NIF; each non-resident shareholder must maintain a Spanish tax representative if they engage in Spanish-source activities. The return is filed at entity level; non-resident ownership details are not entered on Modelo 200 but are disclosed through corresponding information returns (Modelo 232, Modelo 296).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before offset of prior-year tax losses. Computed from accounting profit adjusted by permanent and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL must determine Spanish-source taxable income on a worldwide basis in its capacity as a resident entity. For non-resident parent or group entities, transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected in the taxable base in accordance with the arm's length principle; documentation supporting the adjustment must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses carried forward, capped at 70% of the taxable base for large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 20 million), 25% for taxpayers with turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 20 million, and 50% for entities under the reduced-size regime, with a statutory carryforward period of 5 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses utilized must be reconciled with the 5-year carryforward records. Non-resident shareholders cannot claim the entity's losses. Any loss-offset adjustment affecting the participation value of non-resident ownership is outside the corporate return's field scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate. General rate 25%; reduced-size entities 20%; new entities first two profitable years 15%; certain cooperative entities 20%; entities dedicated to oil exploration or production 48% for the 2023-2025 period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a wholesale distribution SL, apply the general rate of 25% unless the entity qualifies as a reduced-size entity (turnover below EUR 1 million) or a newly created entity in its first two profitable tax periods. Non-resident shareholders do not apply their own rate to the corporate return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International double taxation relief: deduction for taxes paid abroad on income sourced and taxed in foreign countries; deduction for dividends or profits distributed by a foreign entity when double taxation arises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When the Spanish SL receives dividends, interest, or royalties from non-resident related or unrelated parties, the foreign withholding tax may be credited against the Spanish corporate income tax liability subject to the applicable DTA network and the limits of Article 31 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (LIS). Supporting certificates of foreign tax payment must be submitted with the tax records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 00600 (Deducción para evitar la doble imposición económica: dividendos y plusvalías de fuente interna)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic economic double taxation relief for dividends and capital gains arising from qualifying shareholdings in resident Spanish entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies only to internal Spanish shareholding structures. If the non-resident parent holds the Spanish SL directly, this field is generally not applicable to the wholesale trade activity; any qualifying holdings would be considered at the shareholder level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability after applying the tax rate and before tax credits (bonificaciones and deducciones).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculated at entity level. Non-resident status of shareholders does not modify the computation. If DTA relief is claimed, the tax credits are recorded in subsequent boxes (e.g., Box 00582 or 00583).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings and payments on account already made during the tax period, including corporate income tax prepayments (pagos fraccionados) and withholdings on income earned by the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wholesale cross-border payments received may carry foreign withholding taxes; these are not 'retenciones' in Spain but may be claimed as foreign tax credits. The Spanish SL must ensure that Spanish withholding certificates issued on payments to non-resident suppliers are reported via Modelo 216 and reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable after applying withholdings and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The differential quota must be paid by the Spanish SL irrespective of its non-resident shareholders. Late payment of the differential quota triggers the recargo de apremio and interest de demora.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 00641 (Declaración adicional: operaciones con personas o entidades vinculadas)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reference to the separate transfer pricing information return (Modelo 232) where related-party transactions above thresholds must be reported, including transactions with non-resident related parties. This cross-reference is included in Modelo 200.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL engaged in wholesale transactions with non-resident connected parties must attach to its tax records Modelo 232 details on the counterparties, nature of transactions, amounts, transfer pricing method used, and the functional analysis. Modelo 232 is filed separately within the statutory month of March following the tax year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 1% of the tax payable plus an additional 1% for each full month of delay; if the return is filed without payment, a surcharge of 20% of the tax amount (apremio reducido) may apply if settled within specified voluntary periods. Failure to file within the statutory deadline may trigger a flat penalty of EUR 200 plus EUR 20 per month of delay for entities with a tax base above EUR 3,000, or EUR 150 plus EUR 15 per month for smaller entities. Where the tax authority formally requires filing after non-submission, the penalty is 50% of the tax base or between EUR 1,500 and EUR 20,000 depending on the type of omission. Interest de demora accrues at the statutory rate (currently 3.75% for 2025). Incorrect filing resulting in non-payment may be classified as an infracción leve (fine of 50% of the unpaid amount, reduced to 25% upon conformity) or grave (50%-100%).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on distributions made to non-resident shareholders under the general non-resident income tax regime (IRNR). The Spanish SL is obligated to withhold and remit the 19% withholding when distributing dividends to a non-resident beneficial owner that is not resident in an EU member state or a jurisdiction with a DTA. Dividends distributed to EU parent companies may qualify for the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption at 0% if the shareholder holds at least 5% of the capital (or a 5% voting right alternative) for at least one year, subject to anti-abuse rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced withholding tax rates under a DTA, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Spanish paying entity a valid certificate of tax residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction. The certificate, together with a Formo 210 or a specific Formo 211 if the withholding is applied in the self-assessment, must evidence the effective beneficial ownership of the income. Where the DTA rate is lower than the statutory 19%, the Spanish SL may apply the reduced rate at source only when the residence certificate is received prior to the remittance. In the absence of the certificate, the full 19% must be withheld and the non-resident may subsequently claim a refund through the Spanish tax administration by filing Modelo 210 and submitting the TRC, a statement of beneficial ownership, and a specific application conforming to the Spanish DTA MAP procedures. For EU corporate shareholders, the reduced withholding under Directive 2011/96/EU may be applied directly upon submission of Modelo 296 and a statement of eligibility. The Spanish corporate taxpayer files Modelo 216 quarterly to report withholdings made on non-resident incomes, and Modelo 296 annually with the aggregate list of non-resident recipients and the applicable treaty provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) are 19% for royalties and interest paid to non-resident entities (unless derived through a permanent establishment, in which case corporate income tax at 25% applies). Treaty rates vary by jurisdiction: interest and royalties typically range between 0% and 10% depending on the DTA. For example, under bilateral treaties with the US, UK, Germany, France, and the Netherlands, interest generally may be taxed at 0% or 5% and royalties at 5% or 0% subject to limitations on benefits and beneficial ownership tests. The reduced DTA rates apply only upon presentation of the TRC and, for royalties, the non-resident must not have a permanent establishment in Spain to which the IP is effectively connected. The Spanish SL must apply the withholding at source, report via Modelo 216 (quarterly) and Modelo 296 (annual), and retain evidence of the TRC in the tax file.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 in net turnover. Entities with annual turnover above EUR 10 million must maintain transfer pricing documentation comprising both Master File and Local File. For entities with turnover between EUR 1 million and EUR 10 million, only the Local File is mandatory when related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 per related counterparty or EUR 250,000 in total for transactions of the same type. Modelo 232 must be filed when the total amount of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000 per counterparty and type of transaction, or when certain transactions with tax havens occur regardless of amount.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain fully applies the Economic Substance concept through the general anti-abuse rule (cláusula general antielusión) in Article 15 of the LGT, the substance requirements of Tax Treaty limitation on benefits provisions, and the specific rules on entities without economic substance in Article 16 of the LIS (restriction on deductibility of certain intragroup payments). Additionally, as a member of the OECD Inclusive Framework and the EU Code of Conduct Group, the Spanish SL operating as a wholesale distributor of SSD and CPU chips must maintain adequate substance in Spain (own premises, local management, employees with decision-making capacity, and significant treasury functions) to resist recharacterization of the Spanish entity as a shell or a conduit. Although Spain does not have separate standalone Economic Substance Regulations like the UAE/Guernsey, the Substance-based carve-out in the domestic transposition of Pillar Two (for MNEs above EUR 750 million) and the jurisprudence of the Supreme Court on sham companies require real operational substance to claim tax treaty benefits, transfer pricing consistency, and VAT input deductions. A purely administrative booking center or letterbox entity without personnel in Spain, serving as the merchandise owner for CPU/SSD wholesale flows, is highly susceptible to reclassification of income to the residence jurisdiction of the foreign parent or beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting sales revenue from the Modelo 200 corporate income tax return; issuing false invoices or double-use invoices for the wholesale trading of SSD and CPU chips without the physical movement of goods; creating artificial paper trails for cross-border semiconductor transactions that lack economic substance; failing to declare related-party transactions with a Hong Kong, Singapore, or Panama intermediary to avoid transfer pricing scrutiny.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty under Articles 191 and 184 LGT: a monetary penalty equal to 50% of the amount not declared when the omission is detected through an unannounced inspection, with increases to 100% when using invoicing databases or concealed means. If concealment is found (differences between declared and actual amounts exceed EUR 50,000 and also exceed 10% of the declared tax base), the penalty is 100% of the evaded amount. Criminal sanction under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code (Ley Orgánica 10/1995): imprisonment from 1 to 5 years plus a fine of six times the evaded tax and loss of public subsidies or benefits for 3 to 6 years. Tax evasion exceeding EUR 120,000 per year triggers criminal liability. For a wholesale semiconductor distribution entity with substantial turnover, any undisclosed invoice for CPU chips above the EUR 120,000 threshold activates the criminal offense automatically.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers face criminal imprisonment (1 to 5 years) if the evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000. Civil liability for the tax debt under Article 42 LGT (responsabilidad solidaria) arises when directors intentionally or negligently cause the non-payment of the corporate tax liability. The director's personal assets may be seized for the company's tax debt, VAT, and withholding obligations. Travel bans and precautionary suspension of corporate activities may be ordered by the examining judge in criminal tax proceedings. De facto control exercised by beneficial owners from a foreign jurisdiction does not shield them: the Spanish Tax Agency applies the look-through doctrine and criminal courts may extradite or issue European Arrest Warrants for individuals steering the scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Entidad sin Sustancia)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada with no physical office in Spain, no local payroll, no bank account in Spain with decision-making treasury capacity, and using it solely to route sales of SSD and CPU chips to other group entities; claiming treaty benefits or Parent-Subsidiary Directive protection on margins generated by a marketing or purchasing function that has no local personnel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under Article 16 LIS (transactions with related persons) and the general anti-abuse clause (Article 15 LGT). The Tax Agency may integrate the income in the foreign parent's Spanish permanent establishment or deny the Spanish entity's separate personality. The entity may be challenged as a fictitious company under Article 365 of the Commercial Code, and public registries may be instructed to close the registration. Where the shell is used to circumvent EU sanctions or export control restrictions on semiconductors, the sanctions offense triggers criminal liability under LO 10/1995. Penalties for the disregard may reach 100% of the rescheduled corporate tax, plus late-interest. Existence of a nominal administrator (testaferro) causes joint and several liability for all tax debt and could lead to a director disqualification of up to 10 years under the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A Spanish resident director who merely lends his name to a shell SL is jointly and severally liable for the entire tax assessment. If the company is held to be a criminal instrument for money laundering (Article 301 Criminal Code) or fraud to the EU budget, the director's personal criminal liability is triggered and the corporate veil will be pierced. Travel bans are routinely imposed on foreign beneficial owners when criminal proceedings disclose an intent to leave Spain. Directors may be disqualified from setting up new companies for a period of 5 to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Swift_TT wire transfers for wholesale semiconductor transactions without performing KYC on the counterparty; using staged Escrow_Inspection_Wire payment structures to disguise transfers from tax-haven jurisdictions; making or receiving cash payments above €10,000; structuring transactions to stay below reporting thresholds; using layering payments through the SL's accounts in multiple countries; pretending to trade in SSD/CPU chips where the goods are actually scrap metal, counterfeit, or non-existent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanctions under Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing: fines from EUR 60,001 up to EUR 5,000,000 (very serious infraction) for an obligated entity's failure in due diligence or failure to declare suspicious operations through SEPBLAC. Criminal conviction for money laundering under Article 301 of the Criminal Code carries imprisonment from 1 to 6 years and fines of three times the value of the laundered assets. Confiscation of the goods, the corporate bank accounts, and the total profits from the wholesale trading scheme is mandatory. The Spanish Council of Ministers, at the request of the AML Commission, may suspend the entity's authorization and close offices for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are subject to individual criminal liability for each money laundering transaction they authorize or knowingly allow. They may be imprisoned up to 6 years; if the director is part of an organization dedicated to money laundering, the sanction escalates to 3-6 years plus additional disqualification. Travel bans and freezing of personal assets are granted by the Central Investigating Court (Juzgado Central de Instrucción) under the National Court jurisdiction. The beneficial owner (even if non-resident) can be tried under Spanish law and international arrest warrants may be issued. Directors who allow the SL to be used in cross-border predicate offenses such as smuggling of electronic components can also be held criminally liable for a counterfeiting and industrial property infraction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and False Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating the wholesale margin on SSD and CPU trades with related parties in Hong Kong or Switzerland to shift profits out of Spain; charging a 3% mark-up when the Spanish company executes a full entrepreneurial risk-bearing purchase/resale function requiring an 8% return; failing to file Modelo 232; failing to prepare the TP local file despite the EUR 250,000 threshold; signing cross-border contracts with shell subsidiaries that are not the actual decision makers; omitting intra-group services invoices for the chip distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the Tax Agency adjusts the taxable base by applying the arm's length method infringing the documentation duty, the penalty is 15% of the amount of the adjustment, unless the taxpayer has correctly disclosed the transactions in Modelo 232. Non-submission of the documentation itself is sanctioned by EUR 1,000 to EUR 15,000 per data set (Article 198 LGT). Failure to file Modelo 232 is fined at EUR 300 per data missing (up to EUR 6,000) and EUR 1,500 to EUR 30,000 if fully omitted. The adjustment may generate a resulting tax debt with interest. If the adjusted transaction has also been artificially arranged to obtain a tax advantage, a specific penalty of 25% of the amount of the advantage erroneously obtained is imposed for abusive structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the false transfer pricing documentation are considered co-perpetrators of the alleged tax evasion and may face criminal proceedings if the adjustment exceeds EUR 120,000. The corrective assessment, including the 15% surcharge, becomes a debt of the entity, but the director may be held personally liable if he knowingly signed a false affidavit of the functional analysis. Courts have ordered a 30-day travel ban and surrender of passport for administrators charged with transfer pricing fraud where substantial sums were moved to Chinese and Singaporean trading companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misdeclaration in Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Falsa o Inexacta)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming an inflated cost of goods sold by submitting forged proof-of-delivery documents for SSD/CPU shipments that never entered Spain; using purchase orders from a non-existent supplier in a tax haven to reduce the corporate taxable income; failing to include as income custom duties refunds or export subsidies; omitting advance payments received from foreign clients for chip delivery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 184 LGT, a minor infraction (infracción leve) carries a 50% fine of the amount of the misrepresented base, reduced to 25% if the penalty is paid through conformation without appeal. If the misdeclaration is discovered after a formal tax audit, the fine is not reduced and may be accompanied by publication of the sanction in the official gazette. Modelo 200 filing after 25 July without payment triggers a surcharge of 20% to 35%, plus interest. Criminal qualification applies when the amount exceeds EUR 120,000, with prison terms of 1 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The administrator that signs the Modelo 200 is deemed liable for the accuracy of the return. Personal liability under Article 42 LGT, joint and several, applies to those who direct the preparation of false tax data. Directors may be disqualified from receiving EU funds, subsidies, or tax benefits for up to 5 years. Criminal judges may order the embargo (seizure) of personal bank accounts and properties of directors whose forged invoices are part of the scheme.
